task: Turn the esl-likes Drink Stand into a short arcade service rush: shift totals 5/6/7, a pure tested director that keeps windows and the line busy after a short warm-up, a real final ラッシュ！ phase, arrival/success cues and speech-focus audio ducking — without changing the English or regressing anything already validated.
notes: READ FIRST: SPEC.md §3 'Protected speech focus', SPEC.md §6 (especially the rewritten 'Difficulty'), and the last DESIGN_DECISIONS.md entries, especially '2026-09-13 — Rush-hour revision'. Those are the frozen contract; where this brief and SPEC disagree, SPEC wins — say so in your summary.

STABLE BASE — DO NOT REGRESS (validated on the committed build): 1/2/3 windows; hold-to-fill identical at six stations shuffled once per session (pure fill.js: valid at 35%, top-up at the same station, a different drink empties, overflow stays valid, never scored); short tap on the action button latches to full; click a station to walk there and latch; HUD fill glass with valid line, check, full rim, spill; notice tones; wrong drink empties the cup (Japanese refusal, English not repeated, first-try lost, combo breaks); queued customers have no patience countdown; speechFocus service clock freezes every pressure timer; ラッシュ！ banner positioned over the floor band; targetQuestion refuses prompts for anyone but the click-to-walk target; questionCustomerStillNear; Listen Again; turnaround with six drinks; finish() payload; full disposal in exit().

WHY: a fixed five-customer sequence feels finite and predictable. Drink Stand must feel faster than the Restaurant: hear → turn → find → fill → sprint → serve, the player moving almost constantly. It stays immediate: no kitchen delays, no tray, no temperature, no person-order memory beyond the customers at the windows.
SHIFT (frozen numbers): customers per session Easy 5 / Normal 6 / Challenge 7; windows 1 / 2 / 3; every customer is a real asking (no filler customers). Patience values stay as they are.

DIRECTOR: replace the fixed spawnAt timetable and the hard-wired 'last three customers are the rush' with src/minigames/drinkStand/director.js — a PURE module (no DOM, no three.js), rng-injectable, advanced only by service time, e.g. createDrinkDirector({ level, total, windows, rng }) with advance(serviceDt, view) -> events such as { type: 'arrive' } and a phase ('warmup' | 'main' | 'rush'). The controller keeps owning queue/window movement and passes a small view (windows in use, queued count, customers remaining, focusReleasedAgo). Rules: short warm-up (first customer almost at once, the next with a gentler gap, ~8–12 s of service time on Normal/Challenge); main phase keeps windows filled and tops up the line so that when all windows are busy at least one customer is usually waiting; the rush phase begins when the remaining un-arrived customers are the last ~40% of the total (at least 2): arrival gaps shrink to roughly 0.6–1.0 s so the line visibly grows, the ラッシュ！ banner shows, cue sounds quicken. A freed window must be refilled from the line immediately (promotion already exists — keep it fast). After speech focus ends, hold new arrivals ~0.8 s of service time so the child is not ambushed; never hold patience. Guard against queue starvation during the rush and against every window emptying mid-shift on Normal/Challenge. Easy: one window, a modest stream, never frantic.
The director reads only the service clock, so speech focus freezes arrivals, queue promotion walking, patience and rush progression by construction. Do not add per-timer focus guards.

FEEL: an arrival chime when a customer reaches a window; a quick service-success sound; keep dispensing/fizz/overflow sounds; a slightly faster/brighter cue variant during the rush phase; combo pop as today; a small progress counter using formatUi(UI.drinkStand.progress, { done, total }) where done = resolved customers (never a countdown). Call audio.setFocusDuck(true) when focus begins, audio.setFocusDuck(false) when it ends and in exit() (the function exists in src/systems/audio.js; do not modify audio.js). REJECTED, do not add: continuous ambience, footsteps, highlighting the requested station, auto-facing the station, reordering stations mid-session.
STRINGS: UI.drinkStand.progress and UI.drinkStand.rush already exist in src/config/lesson.js. Do not edit lesson.js.

LESSONS FROM THE RESTAURANT INTEGRATION (verified 2026-09-13, apply them here): (1) An open dwelling or committed conversation must outrank every other context branch in updateContext — the Restaurant cleared a committed question whenever a ready dish was in pickup range, which cancelled it and disarmed the dwell so the customer could never be asked; make sure no pour/serve/station/queue context branch can call clearQuestion() while a question is dwelling or committed for a customer still in range. (2) Expose dwell and question state in the debug snapshot exactly like the Restaurant does: dwell: { phase, targetId, progress } and question: { customer, committed }. (3) Harness: a click on a customer may start a walk OR arrive instantly (already standing there) and go straight to the dwell — accept either signal (autoWalking, dwell.targetId, question.customer) and re-click with fresh coordinates if neither appears; wait for question.committed via the debug hook before expecting the mic-free fallback or a mock try-again, because the dwell uses frame time that software GL clamps; and make the 'mic does not reopen while standing still' check require that one automatic session really started first, so it can never pass vacuously. See scripts/playthrough.mjs clickAndWaitForArrival and its silence probe for the working pattern.

HARNESS INFRASTRUCTURE (new, reduces controller rerun cost): (1) Create scripts/lib/driver.mjs with small reusable helpers and use them in scripts/playthrough-drink.mjs: waitForDebug(page, key, predicate, { timeoutMs, label }) returning the snapshot or null; clickUntil(page, getPoint, predicate, { attempts, timeoutMs }) that re-reads coordinates each attempt; holdUntil(page, key | pointer, predicate, { maxMs }) that holds until a state is reached rather than for a fixed duration; a check helper that records PASS/FAIL, supports a required precondition so a check can never pass vacuously, and attaches a compact debug trace to every FAIL; and quiet retries (log a retry only when the final attempt fails, not every timeout). Do not change scripts/playthrough.mjs (Restaurant) to use it in this order. (2) Make scripts/playthrough-drink.mjs section-selectable: parse --only <names> (comma list, e.g. listening,guessing,level2,mic) from process.argv and run only those sections, defaulting to all; scripts/playthrough-run.mjs passes extra arguments through, so `npm run playthrough:drink-stand -- --only mic` must work — verify the runner forwards arguments and, only if it does not, make the smallest additive change there and say so. (3) Every new state machine you add (director phase, dwell, question) must be visible in window.__eslDebug.drinkStand from the start.

DWELL RING VISIBILITY (observed in the Restaurant screenshots): a thin faint arc was easy to miss at 1366x768. The Drink Stand dwell ring must read at a glance: a thick high-contrast arc (for example a white outline with a bright yellow progress stroke, several pixels wide at 1366x768) around or above the window customer, never food- or drink-related, and never covering the English station signs.

DWELL TO TALK (SPEC §3 'Dwell to talk'; the shared foundation is built and the Restaurant already integrates it — read src/systems/talkDwell.js, src/config/interaction.js, speech.listenOnce()/autoListenAllowed() and the Restaurant integration for the pattern; do not modify them and do not extract a shared controller). Replace proximity-opens-prompt: each frame with REAL frame dt call dwell.update(dt, { candidates: customers atWindow && !asked as { id: index, x: approachX, z: approachZ, radiusSq: CUSTOMER_RADIUS_SQ, lookX: WINDOWS[window].x, lookZ: WINDOWS[window].z } — the radius stays on the approach point, but facing MUST be judged toward the customer behind the counter via lookX/lookZ, because the avatar stands on the approach point itself after a click-to-walk, player: { x, z, forwardX: Math.sin(player.rotation.y), forwardZ: Math.cos(player.rotation.y) }, moving: movement input non-zero OR an auto-walk in progress OR a fill in progress, lockedTargetId: the click-to-walk customer's index or null }). While dwelling or ready: a simple progress ring at that window's customer and a slight turn toward the player; show the HUD talk control without focus so a manual hold works. Commit when ready, at once on a manual hold (LISTENING), or when ready in mic-free mode: dwell.commit(), focus.begin(), audio.setFocusDuck(true), a soft ready chime, then speech.listenOnce() only when speech.autoListenAllowed() (otherwise the hold control waits); mic-free shows the fallback at commit. notifyAccepted on acceptance; notifyEnded('failed' | 'cancelled') on try-again or walking away, so the mic never reopens while standing still. Click-to-walk arrival rotates the avatar to face the clicked window customer and dwells with no extra click, but must not spin the avatar so far that the station row stops being the obvious next direction — face the window, nothing more. The camera does NOT move. Serving, filling and Listen Again keep their explicit controls. AUTO_TALK_ENABLED false restores proximity prompts. Playthrough: click/walk and wait for the dwell before expecting the fallback; add one mic-mode check with scripts/lib/mockSpeech.mjs (scripted correct question accepted after dwell; scripted silence → try-again and the mock start counter does not rise while standing still) and a check that walking along the windows without stopping opens no prompt.

DEBUG HOOK: keep all existing window.__eslDebug.drinkStand fields (customers with index/state/window/asked/served/patience/screen, stations with id/screen/interaction, player, cup, fillActive, overflowActive, focusActive, focusScale, serviceElapsed, rushShown, questionIndex, autoTarget, configuredCount, maxWindows) and add phase and progress { done, total }. rushStart may remain as the service time the rush phase began (null before).

UNIT TESTS: src/minigames/drinkStand/director.test.mjs (node:test + node:assert/strict, seeded rng) covering: totals 5/6/7 respected and the shift resolves; advance(0) emits nothing; no arrival inside the post-focus hold; warm-up → main → rush order; the rush materially shortens arrival gaps compared with the main phase; with all windows busy in the main/rush phase a customer is usually queued; Easy never has more than one window in use. Keep fill.test.mjs and scoring tests untouched and passing.

PLAYTHROUGH: update scripts/playthrough-drink.mjs for totals 5/6/7 (session A level 3 listening → three stars, session B level 1 fixed-order guessing → finishes below three stars, session C level 2) and keep every existing check (all-window freeze under focus, Space release does not start a fill, partial hold, top-up until valid, short-tap latch, overflow serves, combo, window limits, Listen Again replay, turnaround, no page errors). Add checks: the totals and phase progression are reported; during the level-3 rush a customer is queued while all three windows are busy at some point; windows refill after a serve. HARNESS PITFALLS from this project: wait for an accepted prompt's fallback buttons to clear before approaching the next customer; judge outcomes from debug-state transitions, not leftover text; loop until a state is reached rather than asserting after a fixed-duration hold (software GL runs the game slower than wall clock); never crash on a missing answer — record a FAIL with screenshot and debug state (the lastAcceptContext diagnostic is already there) and break cleanly.

BEHAVIOURAL ACCEPTANCE is owned by the controller: your sandbox cannot start the preview server, so do not spend time trying to run npm run playthrough. Ensure npm test and npm run build pass and syntax-check the playthrough with node --check. Report behavioralValidation honestly (observed: false). Claude will run the playthrough, probes and a visual pass.
Append a short DESIGN_DECISIONS.md entry only for decisions this brief and SPEC do not cover. Do not rewrite existing entries and do not edit SPEC.md.
